messages:
jess_support: FYI customer (acme-prod) hitting intermittent parse failures when using JSON mode for nested arrays. Client sees "invalid JSON" during post-processing even though API sometimes returns 200. They say it only happens under streaming and with mixed item shapes (some items have an extra 'meta' object).

liam_acme: we actually get a 200 most times but the client JSON.parse fails ~1 in 10 requests. looks like last object in stream is cut off (missing comma or brace). caused retries and extra billing.

jess_support: minimal repro below — please try locally and escalate if you can reproduce.

```
# repro (curl)
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-1","json_mode":true,"stream":true,"prompt":"Produce a JSON array of items with id,name,price","max_tokens":256}'
```

Sample prompt/observed response (malformed due to stream split):

```
[
  {"id":1,"name":"widget","price":9.99,"meta":{"source":"v2"}},
  {"id":2,"name":"gadget","price":12.5}
  {"id":3,"name":"thing","price":5.0}
]
```

Note the missing comma after the second item — in some runs the stream chunk boundary appears mid-token which leaves the client with invalid JSON.

sanjay_engineering: :eyes: Can you attach the raw stream chunks and the x-request-id? If we can see chunk boundaries we can check whether our streamer is dropping a separator when concatenating batches. Also need model variant + quantization and whether batching was enabled.

jess_support: request_id=01F7XAB2. Raw chunks uploaded to ticket 12345 (link). Customer says they were on rwd-large-1 (int8) in us-west1, with batching=on and autoscaling. Billing spike noted because their client retried on parse error.

kate_ml: tagging eng-runtime — this might be a boundary/atomicity issue: our structured/json-mode post-processor may assume items are emitted atomically per chunk. Under batching/continuous streaming that assumption can break.

sanjay_engineering: quick troubleshooting checklist: (1) try same prompt with stream=false to confirm it's a streaming-only failure, (2) reproduce with same model+quant flags, (3) capture raw chunk edges and lengths, (4) try disabling server-side batching to see if it prevents mid-item splits.

liam_acme: we tested stream=false and it was stable. stream=true reproduces ~10% of the time. disabling batching on our side (client-side retry backoff) reduced retries but doesn't fix source.

jess_support: customer asked for an ETA. they prefer a server fix (atomic item boundaries or explicit separators). Temporary mitigation is to use stream=false or use a tolerant client parser.

sanjay_engineering: can someone confirm whether json_mode guarantees item-level atomicity across stream chunks? My understanding: not currently guaranteed — structured mode expects the model to output valid JSON but streaming can split tokens. We should document this.

kate_ml: I'll investigate the kernel/streaming codepath for where separators are inserted. If batching merges partial outputs from multiple GPUs we might be losing an injected comma between batched outputs.

jess_support: added customer billing note to ticket. they want a credit if we can't fix quickly.

sanjay_engineering: next actions: I will try to reproduce with an internal load test with rwd-large-1 int8 and batching enabled (assign to me). Kate, can you follow if I reproduce?

triage-bot: Created issue RED-7881 (P2) and linked support ticket 12345.

kate_ml: if this reproduces, we should consider a short-term platform change to insert a safe separator token between items when json_mode=true and stream=true. Long-term fix: make streaming post-processor aware of partial-item boundaries.

jess_support: customer notified of mitigation (use non-streaming or tolerant parser). will update when engineering confirms.

sanjay_engineering: logging notes: grab x-request-id + raw stream, pipeline debug=streamer:true, batching: true, model: rwd-large-1:int8. also include time window for the requests (we saw spikes at ~2026-03-14T16:22Z).

kate_ml: will schedule a deeper dive tomorrow morning and post results here.

jess_support: thanks team. I'll mark customer follow-up for EOD and request potential credit if fix slips.
